lead.title: Janas runs models larger than RAM by streaming MoE experts from SSD
lead.summary: Janas, a pure-C inference engine, keeps mixture-of-experts models larger than system memory viable by streaming experts from the SSD instead of loading everything. It claims 37 tok/s on Qwen3-Next-80B (48 GB) on a 32 GB laptop and beats llama.cpp across the 13 models compared in Q4_K_M — the clearest sign yet that a laptop's RAM ceiling no longer caps what it can run.

top_stories.title: Intel formally launches GPU D-Series with the D270 inference card, up to 480GB of LPDDR5X
top_stories.summary: At the OCP Global Summit, Intel renamed the Crescent Island accelerator as the GPU D270: Xe3P, 1.3 PFLOPS FP8, 1.5 TB/s bandwidth and up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X in a 350 W air-cooled PCIe card. By banking capacity on cheap LPDDR5X instead of scarce HBM, it attacks inference cost-per-gigabyte — a factor that could eventually feed through to cheaper local and hosted inference.

top_stories.title: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its first agentic frontier models — API-only, no open weights
top_stories.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Wonder for personal and professional agentic work via the Meta Model API and Muse Code subscriptions, breaking with its Llama open-weights lineage. For local users the runnable member of the family stays the Apache-2.0 Muse Glimmer 30B on Hugging Face.

top_stories.title: Amazon in advanced talks to acquire Decart for about $7B to bolster Trainium
top_stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports Amazon is in advanced talks to buy Nvidia-backed Decart, whose software moves AI workloads across different chips, for roughly $7B — part of the push to make Trainium a credible alternative to Nvidia. No deal is signed yet.

top_stories.title: Nvidia in early talks to acquire open-weight startup Reflection AI at a $25B valuation
top_stories.summary: The FT reports Nvidia — already an $800M investor in Reflection AI — is weighing a full acquisition, deeper investment or acquihire of the open-source model startup. A deal would pull one of the more prominent open-weight model labs under Nvidia's umbrella.

items.title: DualQuant: dual-scale, calibration-free weight-and-activation quantization for native 4-bit inference
items.summary: Quantizes both weights and activations at two scales without needing calibration data, aiming to recover the full throughput gains of low-bit formats on native 4-bit accelerators.

items.title: Continually post-training small models via synthetic self-distillation
items.summary: Shows standard self-distillation fails on small models because of weak in-context ability, and proposes synthetic self-distillation that lets latency-critical small models acquire new skills without forgetting old ones.

items.title: ReadKV: query-adaptive quantization lets each decoding query read the KV cache at the precision it needs
items.summary: A progressive KV-code scheme that separates the retained-bit budget from the per-query fetch budget, so cheap tokens read low-precision keys and values and important ones read more.

items.title: Adaptive DHiSparse brings speculative decoding to load-adaptive host-memory KV paging
items.summary: Extends hierarchical sparse KV caches with draft-model speculative decoding and adapts the cache budget to load, targeting long-context serving that runs out of KV memory before GPU throughput does.

items.title: ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs, not recurrent state
items.summary: Unrolls state-space recurrence so decode steps replay cached inputs instead of reading and writing state, cutting state I/O and making speculative-decoding rollback cheap in hybrid models.

items.title: AutoTrust ships JEV-35B: one set of open weights serving both fast and deliberative modes
items.summary: The ~36B Apache-2.0 successor to the Qwen3.8-27B-based JEV-27B landed on the Hub and hit trending within a day (6.2k downloads, 236 likes). Its System 1 + System 2 design answers in one mode and thinks in the other from the same checkpoint.

items.title: OpenBMB refreshes MiniCPM-V-4.7-35B-A3B: a 35B multimodal with 3B active per token
items.summary: The image-text-to-text sparse-activation checkpoint saw active updates through October 12-13 and sits in trending. Exactly this class — 35B total, A3B active — is what actually runs on single-workstation hardware.

items.title: Z.ai announces GLM-Legal, an agentic legal model — but the open-weight claim is disputed
items.summary: GLM-Legal, built on the MIT-licensed GLM-5.3-Flash base, posts a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, 12.5 points above the base. Independent coverage flags that the legal checkpoint's access is gated, so the 'open-weight' framing warrants caution; the Flash base itself remains freely downloadable.

items.title: Ollama v0.40.4-rc0: llama.cpp b11521 bump for decision models and EmbeddingGemma 2
items.summary: The release candidate lifts llama.cpp to b11521 for decision-model and EmbeddingGemma 2 support, adds manifest reuse in inference routes, and fixes MLX speculative rollback, following v0.40.3's `ollama launch` fixes.

items.title: Copilot CLI now discovers models from a running local Ollama instance via /model
items.summary: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.94+ can find and add local Ollama models mid-session, and local sandboxing reached GA across CLI, app and VS Code in GitHub's early-October changelog.

items.title: Open WebUI v0.12.0: realtime voice mode, VRM avatars, admin MFA and computer-agent support
items.summary: The v0.12.0 release adds a realtime voice mode backed by an OpenAI Realtime model, animated avatars, nested groups and Open WebUI Computer agent support through an OpenAI-compatible gateway. Milvus and multi-instance Redis setups need upgrade attention.

items.title: CUDA megakernel hits 140 tok/s on Qwen 3.8 27B on a single RTX 3090 — validated against llama.cpp
items.summary: The follow-up accuracy numbers show KL divergence of 0.0007-0.0009 versus llama.cpp across 1K-96K contexts, confirming the 1.4-1.9x decode speedup is not bought with quality loss. A custom CUDA engine is emerging as a real alternative for this model family.

items.title: Self-hosted n8n: the September security advisories have no CVE IDs and are invisible to npm audit
items.summary: About 26 September n8n advisories are absent from OSV.dev and the GitHub Advisory Database, so npm audit, Dependabot and OSV-Scanner can report vulnerable instances as clean. The fix is to update to 2.41.4+ (stable 2.42.6/2.42.7, beta 2.42.1, or 1.123.83) rather than trust scanner verdicts.

items.title: The Verge starts a local-AI diary: running agents for privacy, and what actually breaks
items.summary: The series runs the open-source Hermes Agent with a 125B Qwen 3.8 Flash Next model (~105 GB) on a 256 GB M5 Ultra Mac Studio. The payoff is private work on sensitive files; the failure modes turned out to be host-level — sleeping Macs killing cron jobs silently — and the testing continues on smaller machines.

items.title: Microsoft opens pre-orders for the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box at about $6,000, shipping October 16
items.summary: The Dev Box (Blackwell RTX GPU plus Grace CPU, 1 petaflop AI compute, 128 GB unified memory) costs roughly $2,000 more than AMD's Ryzen AI Halo box and joins the DGX Spark and Mac Studio as a desk-side local-AI machine — with memory-shortage costs pushing all of them above initial expectations.

items.title: NVIDIA reportedly ending the RTX 5090, reserving GB202 silicon for RTX PRO workstation cards
items.summary: Leaker MEGAsizeGPU claims NVIDIA has stopped allocating GB202 dies to the GeForce RTX 5090, redirecting supply to RTX PRO Blackwell cards. If confirmed, the 32 GB 5090 would be the last consumer card at that capacity — pushing serious local-LLM builders toward workstation cards or unified-memory boxes.
